title: Global research trends and hotspots of artificial intelligence research in spinal cord neural injury and restoration-a bibliometrics and visualization analysis.
authors: Tao, Guangyi; Yang, Shun; Xu, Junjie; Wang, Linzi; Yang, Bin
one_liner_zh: 该文是脊髓神经损伤与修复领域AI研究的文献计量学综述，仅提及转录因子调控网络作为未来方向，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology has made breakthroughs in spinal cord neural injury and restoration in recent years. It has a positive impact on clinical treatment. This study explores AI research's progress and hotspots in spinal cord neural injury and restoration. It also analyzes research shortcomings related to this area and proposes potential solutions. METHODS: We used CiteSpace 6.1.R6 and VOSviewer 1.6.19 to research WOS articles on AI research in spinal cord neural injury and restoration. RESULTS: A total of 1,502 articles were screened, in which the United States dominated; Kadone, Hideki (13 articles, University of Tsukuba, JAPAN) was the author with the highest number of publications; ARCH PHYS MED REHAB (IF = 4.3) was the most cited journal, and topics included molecular biology, immunology, neurology, sports, among other related areas. CONCLUSION: We pinpointed three research hotspots for AI research in spinal cord neural injury and restoration: (1) intelligent robots and limb exoskeletons to assist rehabilitation training; (2) brain-computer interfaces; and (3) neuromodulation and noninvasive electrical stimulation. In addition, many new hotspots were discussed: (1) starting with image segmentation models based on convolutional neural networks; (2) the use of AI to fabricate polymeric biomaterials to provide the microenvironment required for neural stem cell-derived neural network tissues; (3) AI survival prediction tools, and transcription factor regulatory networks in the field of genetics were discussed. Although AI research in spinal cord neural injury and restoration has many benefits, the technology has several limitations (data and ethical issues). The data-gathering problem should be addressed in future research, which requires a significant sample of quality clinical data to build valid AI models. At the same time, research on genomics and other mechanisms in this field is fragile. In the future, machine learning techniques, such as AI survival prediction tools and transcription factor regulatory networks, can be utilized for studies related to the up-regulation of regeneration-related genes and the production of structural proteins for axonal growth.
abstract_zh: 背景：近年来，人工智能（AI）技术在脊髓神经损伤与修复领域取得了突破性进展，对临床治疗产生了积极影响。本研究探讨了AI研究在脊髓神经损伤与修复中的进展与热点，并分析了该领域相关研究不足，提出了潜在解决方案。方法：我们使用CiteSpace 6.1.R6和VOSviewer 1.6.19对Web of Science（WOS）中关于AI在脊髓神经损伤与修复研究中的文章进行了分析。结果：共筛选出1,502篇文章，其中美国占主导地位；Kadone, Hideki（13篇，日本筑波大学）是发表文章数量最多的作者；ARCH PHYS MED REHAB（IF = 4.3）是被引用最多的期刊，主题涵盖分子生物学、免疫学、神经学、运动学等相关领域。结论：我们确定了AI研究在脊髓神经损伤与修复中的三个研究热点：（1）智能机器人和肢体外骨骼辅助康复训练；（2）脑机接口；（3）神经调控和非侵入性电刺激。此外，还讨论了许多新热点：（1）从基于卷积神经网络的图像分割模型入手；（2）利用AI制造聚合物生物材料，为神经干细胞衍生的神经网络组织提供所需微环境；（3）AI生存预测工具，以及遗传学领域的转录因子调控网络。尽管AI研究在脊髓神经损伤与修复中具有诸多益处，但该技术存在若干局限性（数据和伦理问题）。未来研究应解决数据收集问题，这需要大量高质量的临床数据来构建有效的AI模型。同时，该领域基因组学及其他机制的研究较为薄弱。未来，可以利用机器学习技术，如AI生存预测工具和转录因子调控网络，用于与再生相关基因上调和轴突生长结构蛋白产生相关的研究。
